original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Optimistic screen of changed line systems (label window h, rank T, lines v, decoder cost D) under the #4470 joint-helper-lattice invoice with its local word scaled to the new port count and fresh block, and comparison of the resulting break-even lines per dimension with the proven Theorem B cap of research/line-system-saturation.
scope_change_reason: Earlier line-system screens (line-system-saturation x*(h), discussion #3622) used the pre-#4359 break-even fit; under productive helpers the saving is C ~ S/G with fresh-axis work in G, so a shorter window h looked like a large lever (optimistic x1.36..x3.47 for fresh block 7..4 at a fixed lines-per-port ratio). This package checks that lever against the line-count cap.
bottleneck_link: Side result: no new kappa. Tells a new-helper-inventory search which label windows can still pay under the selected accounting.
stop_rule: Stop after the named systems, the Theorem B cap rows h = 3..9 (k = T, 2T, 3T) and the break-even curve h = 3..21; no native word synthesis.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the #4470 targets and paid histograms exactly from RESULT.json local data, checks the root, checks the surplus identity S = (p+2)(v-D) - V exactly on 16 instances, optimises p and a for 14 named systems, the cap rows and the break-even curve, and replays RESULT.json; test_verify.py has 8 positive and rejecting controls.
author: Mark (Matarener)
ai_assistance: Prepared with substantial Claude Code (Claude) assistance.

open_questions.question: Does a saturated even-window system exist at h = 6 (v = 8T, 1 in col of the adjacency) or h = 8 (v = 16T)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These are the only short windows whose Theorem B cap clears the record in this model: h = 6 needs two deleted frames (x1.17 at the cap), h = 8 needs 12.4 lines per dimension against a cap of 16 (x1.46 at the cap).
open_questions.first_step: Extend the realisability numerics of line-system-saturation section 10 to the even-window case with k' = 3 and 4.
open_questions.blocked_by: none; existence of a native word with free central shears on such a unit is a separate, larger obligation

open_questions.question: Is the centre floor D - k (one rank unit saved per deleted line) attainable beyond one deleted frame?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The h = 6 and h = 7 verdicts flip between one and two or three deleted frames; for E8 only P112 and P111 are built and P104 (k = 2T) is still open.
open_questions.first_step: State the deletion rule for E7 analogous to the E8 PR968 floor and test it on the 63-line unit.
